## Solution

The initial condition is
$$u(x,0)=\frac{e^{2x}-1}{e^{2x}+1}=\tanh x=:f(x),$$
which is an odd, bounded function with $|f|\le 1$.

**Heat kernel representation.** The solution of $u_t=u_{xx}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with initial data $f$ is
$$u(x,t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi t}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-(x-y)^2/(4t)}f(y)\,dy=\mathbb{E}\bigl[f\!\left(x+\sqrt{2t}\,Z\right)\bigr],\qquad Z\sim N(0,1).$$
Hence
$$u(1,t)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\tanh\!\left(1+\sqrt{2t}\,Z\right)\bigr].$$

**Symmetry reduction.** Decompose
$$\tanh(1+s)=\tanh s+h(s),\qquad h(s):=\tanh(1+s)-\tanh s=\int_{s}^{s+1}\operatorname{sech}^{2}(r)\,dr.$$
Since $\tanh$ is odd and $Z$ is symmetric,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\tanh\!\left(\sqrt{2t}\,Z\right)\bigr]=0,$$
so
$$u(1,t)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[h\!\left(\sqrt{2t}\,Z\right)\bigr].$$

**Exponential decay of $h$.** Using $\operatorname{sech}^{2}(r)=\dfrac{4}{(e^{r}+e^{-r})^{2}}\le 4e^{-2|r|}$,
$$|h(s)|\le\int_{s}^{s+1}\operatorname{sech}^{2}(r)\,dr\le 4\int_{s}^{s+1}e^{-2|r|}\,dr\le C\,e^{-2|s|}$$
for a universal constant $C$ (the last inequality follows by checking $s\ge0$, $s\le -1$, and $-1\le s\le 0$ separately). Therefore
$$|u(1,t)|\le C\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{-2\sqrt{2t}\,|Z|}\right].$$

**Evaluating the Gaussian expectation.**
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{-2\sqrt{2t}\,|Z|}\right]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-2\sqrt{2t}\,z-z^{2}/2}\,dz.$$
Completing the square, $-z^{2}/2-2\sqrt{2t}\,z=-\tfrac{(z+2\sqrt{2t})^{2}}{2}+4t$, so
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{-2\sqrt{2t}\,|Z|}\right]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{4t}\int_{2\sqrt{2t}}^{\infty}e^{-w^{2}/2}\,dw=2e^{4t}\,\Phi\!\left(-2\sqrt{2t}\right),$$
where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. The standard tail bound $\Phi(-a)\le\dfrac{e^{-a^{2}/2}}{a\sqrt{2\pi}}$ with $a=2\sqrt{2t}$ gives
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{-2\sqrt{2t}\,|Z|}\right]\le 2e^{4t}\cdot\frac{e^{-4t}}{2\sqrt{2t}\cdot\sqrt{2\pi}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi t}}.$$

**Conclusion.**
$$|u(1,t)|\le\frac{C}{2\sqrt{\pi t}}\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{}0.$$

Since $|u(1,t)|\to 0$, we obtain
$$\boxed{\lim_{t\to\infty}u(1,t)=0}.$$
